chains.title: GABPA binds the C250T-created ETS site and activates TERT

links.claim: GABPA is the leading ETS-family candidate to bind the alt A allele more strongly: C250T creates a de novo ETS motif, and GABPA/GABPB1 have been reported to activate the mutant TERT promoter in glioblastoma and bladder cancer. GABPA is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines, but GABPA ChIP peaks containing this variant are only in non-glioblastoma ENCODE biosamples, and no GABPA QBiC-SELEX model is provided, so alt-A preference is inferred rather than directly measured.

The variant lies in the promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with DNase, H3K27ac, and H3K4me3 signal, consistent with an active promoter element; the z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
TERT is the nearest gene, 0 kb from its TSS, and the variant is annotated as upstream of TERT in a TERT promoter regulatory feature.

Glioblastoma is a plausible matched context because GABPA is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines and GABPA/GABPB1 have been implicated at the mutant TERT promoter in glioblastoma and bladder cancer.

If alt-enhanced GABPA binding activates this promoter, it should increase TERT/telomerase; GABPA/GABPB1 activation of the mutant TERT promoter and telomerase has been reported in these tumors, and TERT promoter mutations are a primary cause of telomerase reactivation.

predictions: Recombinant GABPA/GABPB1 or allele-specific GABPA ChIP shows stronger binding to the alt A allele at chr5:1295135.
GABPA or GABPB1 knockdown reduces TERT expression or C250T reporter activity in glioblastoma cells.
The alt allele increases TERT expression in a GABPA-dependent manner in C250T-heterozygous cancer cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP, EMSA, or reporter assay shows no alt-A preference at chr5:1295135.
GABPA or GABPB1 knockdown does not reduce TERT expression or mutant TERT promoter activity in C250T-containing glioblastoma cells.
GABPA occupancy at this base is not detectable in glioblastoma despite an active local promoter.

chains.title: ETS1 with non-canonical NF-kB binds the C250T ETS site and activates TERT

links.claim: ETS1 is an alternative ETS-family candidate because C250T creates an ETS motif and C250T mutant TERT promoter activation has been reported to involve ETS1/2 together with non-canonical NF-kB signalling. No ETS1 QBiC-SELEX model or matched glioblastoma ChIP occupancy at this base is provided, so alt-A preference is literature/motif-inferred and weak.
The variant lies in the active promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 marked by DNase, H3K27ac, and H3K4me3.
TERT is the nearest promoter-proximal gene, 0 kb from its TSS, with the variant upstream of TERT.

The glioblastoma context for ETS1 is not directly established by the provided expression or occupancy data; this chain relies on broader TERT/cancer literature and is therefore weaker than H1 at the cell-type step.
If ETS1/NF-kB cooperatively activates the C250T promoter, alt-enhanced ETS1 binding should raise TERT/telomerase and support tumor proliferation.

predictions: Allele-specific ETS1 ChIP shows stronger binding to the alt A allele at this base.

Recent mechanistic explorations have revealed important roles for TERT promoter mutations and aberrant methylation in activation of TERT transcription and telomerase in UCs.

Point mutations in the core promoter region of the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) gene have been found to occur at high frequencies in several tumour types and considered a primary cause of telomerase reactivation in cancer cells.

These mutations promote TERT gene expression by multiple mechanisms, including the generation of novel binding sites for nuclear transcription factors, displacement of negative regulators from DNA G-quadruplexes, recruitment of epigenetic activators and disruption of long-range interactions between TERT locus and telomeres.

The genomic alterations of the TERT loci including TERT promoter's gain-of-function mutations, copy number gain, fusion and rearrangements, have recently been identified in TCs as mechanisms to induce TERT expression and to activate telomerase.
